title: Adelaide Hall's three pianists in Omaha; pushing players off jobs
summary: In Omaha around 1930 he hears Adelaide Hall with Art Tatum and Joe Turner and describes switching between piano and drums to take jobs.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: mistake in my life, as I tried to tell you, is when Adelaide Hall came to Omaha, Nebraska; Joe Turner on the piano; Art Tatum on the piano. She had three pianists. You must remember in these areas the only way a black person beside Dan and Eddie which were European that worked - they were two black men that worked in tuxedos - when you played the RKO or the Keith's circuit or the Pantages circuit, you had to put on a bandanna, you see. There had to be a cotton scene. But these people came over with class. Here's a woman, Adelaide Hall, came up with 3 pianists. Joe Turner, Art Tatum, and the other pianist - I'll have to go to Europe and try to find out this guy's name. I should know him but - but these are the only two people impressed me in the . But I felt sorry for Art Tatum and since I went to work at 11 o'clock on my piano job, because at this time I would switch from the piano to the drum -

In Omaha. When I found a piano player that was limpid, I'd go and push him off the job. But here comes some hobo would push me off the job. So I'd go around the corner and find me a weak drummer and push him off the job. And here would come another drummer would push me off the job.
